Senses.PreferredTarget: to have sinew in one’s eye
Senses.Note: To have sinew in one’s eye is to possess the discernment demanded by an encounter. Zhangxue Tongzui tells anyone who has it to cover the ears and leave; Linquan Conglun makes it the condition for seeing that his tongue has said nothing; Hongzhi grants an interlocutor’s line only on that condition.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To have sinew in one’s eye is to possess the discernment demanded by an encounter. Zhangxue Tongzui tells anyone who has it to cover the ears and leave; Linquan Conglun makes it the condition for seeing that his tongue has said nothing; Hongzhi grants an interlocutor’s line only on that condition.
EvidenceBody: A bodily sinew becomes the eye’s capacity to discriminate a live turn from verbal display, and its presence is tested by what the hearer does next.
The phrase does not describe anatomy in these cases; every witness uses it as an appraisal of discernment.
Instruction, case-comment condition, and qualified approval all predicate the same discerning capacity.
